name: Montana

events.title: Statehood
events.text: Montana became the 41st state on November 8, 1889. Congress gave it 1 seat in the House until the next apportionment.

events.title: 1890 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1890 census, Montana kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 1900 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1900 census, Montana kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 1910 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1910 census, Montana's House delegation grew from 1 to 2 seats.

events.title: Statewide (general ticket) elections
events.text: In the 63rd through 65th Congresses (1913–1919), Montana elected all of its representatives statewide on a general ticket instead of by district.

events.title: 1930 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1930 census, Montana kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1940 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1940 census, Montana kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1950 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1950 census, Montana kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1960 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1960 census, Montana kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: Districting commission created
events.text: Montana's 1972 constitution gave redistricting to a five-member citizen commission: legislative leaders each pick one member, those four pick a chair, and no member may be a public official. It draws both congressional and legislative districts.

events.title: 1970 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1970 census, Montana kept 2 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 1980 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1980 census, Montana kept 2 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: Montana loses its challenge
events.text: After the 1990 census cut Montana to one seat, the state sued over the formula used to divide seats among states. The Supreme Court upheld the method of equal proportions in United States Department of Commerce v. Montana.

events.title: 1990 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1990 census, Montana's House delegation shrank from 2 to 1 seat. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 2000 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2000 census, Montana kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 2010 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2010 census, Montana kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: Two districts again
events.text: After the 2020 census gave Montana a second seat, the commission's chair broke a deadlock between the other four members to advance a proposal. The commission gave final approval to an east–west two-district map on November 12, 2021.

events.title: 2020 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2020 census, Montana's House delegation grew from 1 to 2 seats. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

compactnessNote: Polsby-Popper compactness (4π × area ÷ perimeter²) measured on the projected district shapes. It describes shape only: coastlines, rivers and county lines lower it too, so a low score is not evidence of intent. "Irregular" marks the least compact 5% of district shapes in each census era nationally.

c066.text: Montana's district lines were redrawn between censuses, first used in the 1918 election. The reason has not been researched yet.

c090.text: Montana's district lines were redrawn between censuses, first used in the 1966 election. The reason has not been researched yet.

c093.text: New map drawn after the 1970 census, which left Montana with 2 seats. It was first used in the 1972 election.

c099.text: New map drawn after the 1980 census, which left Montana with 2 seats. It was first used in the 1984 election.

c103.text: New map drawn after the 1990 census, which cut Montana's seats from 2 to 1. It was first used in the 1992 election.

c118.text: New map following: Two districts again. After the 2020 census gave Montana a second seat, the commission's chair broke a deadlock between the other four members to advance a proposal. The commission gave final approval to an east–west two-district map on November 12, 2021.
